title: Namibia calculator readiness research — Batch 32
executive_summary: Batch 32 added the NAB 5 June 2026 Grade 1 mahangu floor-price notice and its standardized rain-fed cost annexure. The farm-gate/collection-centre floor price is N$7.87407/kg; the mill-door price is N$8.16672/kg. The annexure is a mahangu-specific benchmark, not a multi-crop or region-specific budget. FAO's 28 August 2026 outlook estimates aggregate cereal output at 155,000 tonnes; no crop-level allocation is inferred.

sources.use: 2024/25 marketed grain volumes by six zones, selected zone-level yields, annual floor-price averages.
2026 aggregate cereal estimate 155,000 tonnes; commercial share nearly 80%; communal cereal output below average; improved livestock body conditions; Zambezi locust/flood losses.

sources.publisher: Namibia Ministry of Urban and Rural Development

sources.use: 2026 Grade 1 mahangu farm-gate and mill-door floor prices plus itemized standardized rain-fed production-cost annexure.

safeguards: NAB agronomic zones are not administrative regions.
Marketed grain volumes are not total production or yield.
Annual floor-price averages are not dated farm-gate transaction prices.
FAO aggregate cereal production is not apportioned among individual crops.
Namibia remains directory-only; original 10 active countries are not changed.
2026 Grade 1 mahangu floor prices apply only to the 2026 marketing season; the farm-gate/collection-centre price already deducts producer levy and producer transport share.
The NAB rain-fed mahangu cost annexure is not a representative multi-region budget and must not be generalized to other crops.
remaining_work: Extract NSA 2026 agriculture bulletin tables and final 2025/26 Census of Agriculture outputs.
Verify NAB zone-level yield observations, especially the unusually low Zambezi value, and build a documented zone-to-region crosswalk.
Obtain current dated producer prices and farmer-paid input costs by region and production system for all calculator commodities.

Build representative irrigated and rain-fed budgets and calculator test cases.
